metadata.description: Pathfinder Conversation Guide Questions with KA/iKA/FA/MA alignment scoring - Updated from PDF specifications

ka.name: Kinematic Alignment
ka.description: Kinematic Alignment prioritizes restoration of each patient's native joint line
ka.fullDescription: Kinematic alignment prioritizes restoration of each patient's native joint line and pre-disease anatomy. The femur is resurfaced first to match the native distal and posterior joint lines. The tibia is then resurfaced to restore is pre-arthritic orientation. Femoral and tibial resection depths are planned to match implant thickness, accounting for cartilage and bone wear, with the goal of reproducing native knee kinematics and minimizing the need for soft-tissue releases. [9][10][11][12]

ika.name: Inverse Kinematic Alignment
ika.description: Inverse Kinematic Alignment aims to resurface the proximal tibia back to its pre-arthritic state
ika.fullDescription: Inverse Kinematic Alignment aims to resurface the proximal tibia back to its pre-arthritic state. The tibial resection thickness assumes the minimum tibial insert is used and is equal to implant thickness minus cartilage and bone wear. The tibia is resurfaced, and osteophytes are resected. The soft tissues of the knee are assessed using the CAS tensioner and ACCUBALANCE Graph before proceeding with the femoral resections. The femoral resection depth and angulations are planned in a way to balance gaps using the ACCUBALANCE Graph and obtain the intended soft tissue balance of the knee. [20]

fa.name: Functional Alignment
fa.description: Functional alignment aims to provide balanced flexion-extension gaps
fa.fullDescription: Functional alignment aims to provide balanced flexion-extension gaps. The Functional Alignment planning method enables adjustments in the coronal plane for both the distal femoral and proximal tibial resections to achieve the desired soft tissue laxity symmetry on the ACCUBALANCE Graph. [18]

ma.name: Mechanical Alignment
ma.description: Mechanical Alignment with balancing targets a neutral hip-knee-ankle (HKA) axis
ma.fullDescription: Mechanical alignment with balancing targets a neutral hip-knee-ankle (HKA) axis. Bone resections are planned perpendicular to the mechanical axes of the femur and tibia. The femoral component position may then be adjusted to balance flexion and extension gaps, with tibial resection depth modified if needed. This technique prioritizes minimizing femoral and tibial deviation from neutral alignment. [1][2][3]

questions.question: How do you sequence your resections during total knee arthroplasty (TKA)?

options.text: Femur First
Tibia First

questions.question: What do you prioritize when performing Total Knee Arthroplasty (TKA)?

options.text: Neutral mechanical alignment (0° HKA)
Restoring the patient's native alignment
Prioritizing balanced flexion and extension gaps

questions.question: Do you adjust your resections to balance the soft tissue?

options.text: Yes
No

questions.question: Are you willing to deviate from mechanical axis (0° HKA)?

options.text: Yes
No
Be used to balance - adjusts the femoral resection within boundaries to obtain the target gaps
Be perpendicular to mechanical axis - the femoral resection is aligned perpendicular to the femur's mechanical axis
Restore native joint line obliquity - the femoral resection is positioned to restore the joint line to pre-arthritic position
Be used to balance – adjusts the tibial resection within boundaries to obtain the target gaps
Be perpendicular to mechanical axis - the tibial resection is aligned perpendicular to the tibia's mechanical axis
Restore native joint line obliquity - the tibial resection is positioned to restore the joint line to pre-arthritic position

questions.question: When balancing extension gaps, the priority is:

options.text: Minimize tibial varus - prioritizes neutral tibia, adjusts femur component to balance extension gaps
Minimize femoral joint line deviation - prioritizes native femur joint line, adjusts tibia component to balance gaps
Evenly distributes changes to femur/tibia, varus/valgus adjustments made between both components to balance gaps.
Restore both medial and lateral posterior condylar offsets - both medial and lateral posterior resections aim to recreate the pre-arthritic posterior condylar offset

Restore medial posterior condylar offset and use lateral resection to balance - the medial posterior resection recreates the pre-arthritic medial posterior condylar offset, and the lateral posterior resection is used to balance gaps
Use both medial and lateral resections to balance - both medial and lateral posterior resections are used to balance gaps to obtain the intended ligament tension

questions.question: Do you apply coronal boundaries (limits to deviation)?

options.text: Yes
No
